content.thinking:
Reviewing event types, issue events, and webhook delivery.

Evaluating whether to persist projectId on notification rows for digest filtering. Reviewing mute table patterns in other repositories.

Decided to store projectId directly on notification rows. This lets digests exclude muted projects and re-include them after unmute. The Notification type and database column will both gain a project_id field. Existing tests that construct notification objects may need updates.

Settled on an optional `projectId` field to avoid breaking tests that manually construct notification objects. The task explicitly permits updating visible tests that encode altered behavior.

The comment.created event is missing a projectId.

The projectId for comment.created must be fetched from the linked issue. Other issue and comment events already include it.

Personal notification kinds are created but never include the email channel. Digests filter out muted projects and require projectId on each notification. Webhooks are handled separately from member mutes.

NewNotification is defined as an Omit type derived from Notification.

Making projectId required on Notification would break the digest test's insert. The field will remain optional instead. The task requires updating visible tests that encode this behavior.

Checking the return type of `findIssueById` for `projectId`.

Defining personal notification kinds. Mute logic will strip emails from channels for personal issues when a projectId is present, and skip non-personal issues. Digests will filter muted project IDs per recipient.
Checking tests that construct Notification objects as full types. The toNotification change is fine if projectId is on the type and the mapper sets it.

content.thinking:
Project mutes will be added to the notifications schema file.

listMutedProjectIds will return a readonly ProjectId array. Unmute is idempotent and ignores missing records. The actor needs project:read permission. Checks run in this order: tenant scope, project existence, then permission. Mute and unmute follow the same sequence. Whether list should also enforce org scope is still being considered.

listMutedProjectIds will enforce org scope with TenantScopeError for consistency. It will not require project:read permission, so it returns all muted project IDs regardless of current access.

A new `applyMute` helper will strip email channels from personal notifications like issue assignments and overdue issues when muted. If no channels remain after filtering, it returns null.

Webhook channels are treated as workspace deliveries rather than member notification channels, so personal mutes only remove email while leaving webhooks intact.

The digest pipeline will filter out muted projects before applying the result cap, ensuring the cap applies to the remaining notifications.

I'll implement the project mute repository in notification-preference or a new file.

A dedicated `project-mute-repository.ts` file is cleaner. The schema will use a unique composite index on org_id, user_id, and project_id. It will stay minimal with just those three fields and no timestamps.

The Drizzle schema will omit an id column and rely on the unique composite index. The list query will return ProjectId branded values.

A `requireReadableProject` helper will enforce org scope and read permissions. The list endpoint will simply delegate to the mute repository after confirming tenant scope.

The list endpoint will only verify org scope, not require notification:read. Mute checks will only run when a payload actually contains a projectId. The digest service will import the mute repository directly rather than using an actor, since it only has a recipientId. Filtering muted recipients will use a Set loaded from the repository.
Checking whether tests use an in-memory Drizzle schema or migrate SQL.
runMigrations uses SQL files in the migrations directory when they exist.
